components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 这家公司的总部设在上海。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de zǒngbù shè zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: This company's headquarters is located in Shanghai.
example.fact: 总 (built from 口 “mouths” over 心 “heart, mind” — many voices gathered under one mind) contributes the sense of “overall, chief”; attached to 部 (“department, section”), 总部 names the one central department that oversees all the others — literally the “chief branch.”

examples.hanzi: 这家银行的总部在北京。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng de zǒngbù zài Běijīng.
examples.english: This bank's headquarters is in Beijing.

examples.hanzi: 他被调到总部工作了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi diào dào zǒngbù gōngzuò le.
examples.english: He was transferred to work at the headquarters.

meanings: woman of similar age to one's parents

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
女 (woman) — marks female relatives and women, as in 妈 mum, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姨 is mother's sister.
夷 (yí) gives the sound exactly: 姨 yí.

example.hanzi: 楼下的阿姨每天都会来打扫。
example.pinyin: Lóu xià de āyí měitiān dōu huì lái dǎsǎo.
example.english: The auntie downstairs comes to clean every day.
example.fact: Beyond its literal sense of “maternal aunt,” 阿姨 has become the standard polite way to address any adult woman of roughly one's parents' age or a woman doing domestic or childcare work — much as 叔叔 (“uncle”) extends the same courtesy to men, letting speakers avoid a stranger's real name or a more distancing title.

examples.hanzi: 阿姨，请问洗手间在哪里？
examples.pinyin: Āyí, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Auntie, excuse me, where is the restroom?

examples.hanzi: 我阿姨在医院当护士。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ āyí zài yīyuàn dāng hùshi.
examples.english: My aunt works as a nurse in the hospital.

meanings: to bring out implicit or innate qualities

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 挥 is to wave or wield.
军 (jūn) — near sound — 挥 is huī; 军 also sounds out 辉 huī.

example.hanzi: 他在比赛中充分发挥了自己的水平。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng chōngfèn fāhuī le zìjǐ de shuǐpíng.
example.english: He fully displayed his ability in the competition.
example.fact: 挥 pictures a hand 扌 giving a commanding wave, built on the phonetic 军 (“army”); combined with 发 (“to emit, send out”), 发挥 suggests something like “sending out with a wave of the hand” — an image that maps neatly onto its modern sense of bringing out hidden potential or ability.

examples.hanzi: 这个演员的表现很好，充分发挥了自己的才能。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yǎnyuán de biǎoxiàn hěn hǎo, chōngfèn fāhuī le zìjǐ de cáinéng.
examples.english: This actor performed very well and made full use of his talent.

examples.hanzi: 考试时，别紧张，好好发挥。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì shí, bié jǐnzhāng, hǎohāo fāhuī.
examples.english: Don't be nervous during the exam; just do your best.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.hanzi: 这份文件属于国家机密。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn shǔyú guójiā jīmì.
example.english: This document is classified as a state secret.
example.fact: 机 (originally a wooden mechanism or device, such as a loom — from 木 “wood” plus 几, a stool-like shape) and 密 (a quiet, secluded place under a roof) combine into something close to “a hidden mechanism,” fitting 机密's modern sense of classified, need-to-know information.

examples.hanzi: 这些机密不能告诉任何人。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē jīmì bù néng gàosu rènhé rén.
examples.english: You can't tell anyone these secrets.

examples.hanzi: 他泄露了公司的机密。
examples.pinyin: Tā xièlòu le gōngsī de jīmì.
examples.english: He leaked the company's confidential information.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
角 (horn, corner) — a picture of an animal horn. Read jiǎo for horn, corner and angle; jué for a role, as in 角色.

example.hanzi: 她是这部电影的女主角。
example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè bù diànyǐng de nǚ zhǔjué.
example.english: She is the female lead of this movie.
example.fact: 角 is a pictograph of a ridged animal horn, later extended metaphorically to mean a dramatic “role” or “character” — much as English “horn” has no connection to acting, Chinese theater borrowed an unrelated physical object to name a stage part, and 主角 simply marks that role as the “main” (主) one.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的主角是一位年轻的医生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de zhǔjué shì yí wèi niánqīng de yīshēng.
examples.english: The lead role in this movie is a young doctor.

examples.hanzi: 在这个故事里，小狗才是主角。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhège gùshi lǐ, xiǎo gǒu cái shì zhǔjué.
examples.english: In this story, the puppy is the real protagonist.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
女 (woman) — marks women and grace, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 娜 is graceful, used in female names.
那 (nà) gives the sound: 娜 is nuó or nà, like 挪 nuó.

example.hanzi: 安娜是我最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Ānnà shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: Anna is my best friend.
example.fact: 安娜 is a pure phonetic transliteration of the foreign name “Anna” — 安 (“peace, safety”) and 娜 (a character reserved almost exclusively for women's names) were chosen for their sound alone, not their meaning, the same strategy behind most transliterated foreign names in Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 安娜每天早上都去公园散步。
examples.pinyin: Ānnà měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.english: Anna takes a walk in the park every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我下周要去看安娜，你想一起去吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià zhōu yào qù kàn Ānnà, nǐ xiǎng yìqǐ qù ma?
examples.english: I'm going to see Anna next week; do you want to come along?

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 纪 first meant the thread end, then keeping record, as in 世纪.
己 (jǐ) — same sound, different tone — 纪 is jì; 己 also sounds out 记 jì.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".

example.hanzi: 我们买了一份礼物来纪念这个特别的日子。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen mǎi le yí fèn lǐwù lái jìniàn zhège tèbié de rìzi.
example.english: We bought a gift to commemorate this special day.
example.fact: 纪 (thread radical 纟 plus the phonetic 己) originally referred to keeping silk threads in order, extending to “record, era,” while 念 (今 “the present” over 心 “heart, mind”) means “to keep in mind” — together 纪念 suggests literally “recording in mind,” the mental act of holding onto a memory.

examples.hanzi: 这座塔是为了纪念英雄而建的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò tǎ shì wèile jìniàn yīngxióng ér jiàn de.
examples.english: This tower was built to honor the heroes.

examples.hanzi: 这张照片是我们旅行的纪念。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn shì wǒmen lǚxíng de jìniàn.
examples.english: This photo is a memento of our trip.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 这个品牌在全球都很有名。
example.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái zài quánqiú dōu hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: This brand is famous all over the world.
example.fact: 球 (built from 王, a variant of 玉 “jade,” plus the phonetic 求) originally named a round piece of carved jade before broadening to any “ball, sphere” — so 全球, literally “the whole ball,” treats the Earth as just another sphere, the same everyday metaphor English makes when it calls the planet “the globe.”

examples.hanzi: 全球气候正在变暖。
examples.pinyin: Quánqiú qìhòu zhèngzài biàn nuǎn.
examples.english: The global climate is getting warmer.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏在全球有上亿玩家。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì zài quánqiú yǒu shàng yì wánjiā.
examples.english: This game has hundreds of millions of players worldwide.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: to look carefully inside.
祭 (jì) is a loose sound clue for chá; 祭 also sounds out 际 jì and 擦 cā.
尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.hanzi: 他被带到了警察局做记录。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi dài dào le jǐngchájú zuò jìlù.
example.english: He was taken to the police station to give a statement.
example.fact: 警察局 stacks three meaning-bearing pieces — 警 (“to warn, alert”), 察 (“to observe, inspect”), and 局 (“bureau, office”) — into one compound; the first two alone, 警察, already form the standalone word for “police,” so 局 is simply appended to name the institution or building where they're based.

examples.hanzi: 警察局离我家不远。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchájú lí wǒ jiā bù yuǎn.
examples.english: The police station is not far from my home.

examples.hanzi: 我去警察局报了案。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù jǐngchájú bào le àn.
examples.english: I went to the police station to report the case.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).
雨 (rain) — marks weather and damp, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 雾 fog; 霉 is mould that grows in damp weather.
每 (měi) hints at the sound: 霉 méi is close, and 梅 méi shares 每.

example.hanzi: 今天真倒霉,手机丢了。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān zhēn dǎoméi, shǒujī diū le.
example.english: Today is really unlucky — I lost my phone.
example.fact: 霉 pairs the “rain” radical 雨 with the phonetic 每 (měi) — dampness being the condition mold needs to grow — so 倒霉 literally suggests something like “mold has fallen [on you],” a vivid image behind Mandarin's everyday word for bad luck.

examples.hanzi: 他真倒霉，刚出门就下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhēn dǎoméi, gāng chū mén jiù xià yǔ le.
examples.english: He is so unlucky; it started raining just as he went out.

examples.hanzi: 我这几天特别倒霉，什么都不顺。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhè jǐ tiān tèbié dǎoméi, shénme dōu bú shùn.
examples.english: I've been very unlucky these days and nothing goes right.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胸 is the chest.
匈 (xiōng) gives the sound exactly: 胸 xiōng.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了他的胸部。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le tā de xiōngbù.
example.english: The doctor examined his chest.
example.fact: 部 (built from 阝, a variant of 邑 “settlement,” plus the phonetic 咅) generally marks off a “section” of something larger — attached to a body-part character, it turns a plain noun into a more clinical, anatomical term for that region, the same pattern behind 头部 (“head area”) and 腰部 (“waist area”).

examples.hanzi: 他的胸部受了伤，需要住院治疗。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiōngbù shòu le shāng, xūyào zhùyuàn zhìliáo.
examples.english: His chest was injured and he needs hospital treatment.

examples.hanzi: 她说胸部有点疼，想做个检查。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō xiōngbù yǒudiǎn téng, xiǎng zuò ge jiǎnchá.
examples.english: She said her chest hurts a bit and wants to get checked.

components.note: 心 (heart) — loyalty is of the heart, as in 想 think, 爱 love, 思; 心 sits at the bottom.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound exactly: 忠 zhōng, also in 钟 zhōng.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 请; 诚 is honest speech.
成 (chéng) — same sound — 诚 is chéng, like 成; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng.

example.hanzi: 这只狗对主人非常忠诚。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu duì zhǔrén fēicháng zhōngchéng.
example.english: This dog is extremely loyal to its owner.
example.fact: 忠 (心 “heart” plus the phonetic 中, zhōng — an exact sound match) and 诚 (讠 “speech” plus the phonetic 成, chéng — also an exact match) both combine a semantic radical with a phonetic that doubles as a perfect rhyme, a case where the character's sound-and-meaning construction is unusually transparent even after thousands of years.

examples.hanzi: 他对朋友非常忠诚。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou fēicháng zhōngchéng.
examples.english: He is very loyal to his friends.

examples.hanzi: 忠诚是婚姻中最重要的东西之一。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngchéng shì hūnyīn zhōng zuì zhòngyào de dōngxi zhī yī.
examples.english: Loyalty is one of the most important things in marriage.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 胡 first meant the flesh hanging under the chin.
古 (gǔ) — near sound — 胡 is hú; 古 also sounds out 湖 hú and 糊 hú.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 爷爷留着一把白胡子。
example.pinyin: Yéye liú zhe yì bǎ bái húzi.
example.english: Grandpa has a full white beard.
example.fact: 胡 (⺼ “flesh,” originally the flesh under an animal's chin or throat, plus the phonetic 古) extended from “the area under the chin” to name what grows there — the beard — while 子 acts as a light, meaning-thin noun suffix, the same way it attaches to 桌子 (“table”) and 房子 (“house”).

examples.hanzi: 爸爸刮了胡子，看起来年轻多了。
examples.pinyin: Bàba guā le húzi, kàn qǐlái niánqīng duō le.
examples.english: Dad shaved his beard and looks much younger.

examples.hanzi: 那个男人留着很长的胡子。
examples.pinyin: Nàge nánrén liú zhe hěn cháng de húzi.
examples.english: That man has a very long beard.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 劲 is energy and force.
又 (hand) — 又 here stands in for the older 巠, which gave the near sound: 经 jīng, 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 他干活很有劲。
example.pinyin: Tā gànhuó hěn yǒu jìn.
example.english: He works with a lot of energy.
example.fact: 劲 is the colloquial word for strength and vigor: 有劲 (energetic, or fun), 没劲 (boring, or without energy), 使劲 (to exert effort). Read jìng, it is an adjective meaning 'strong', as in 强劲 (powerful).

examples.hanzi: 他今天干劲十足。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān gànjìn shízú.
examples.english: He is full of energy today.

examples.hanzi: 你使劲推一下门。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shǐjìn tuī yíxià mén.
examples.english: Push the door hard.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.

example.hanzi: 今天的天气很恶劣。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì hěn èliè.
example.english: The weather today is terrible.
example.fact: 恶 is read è in 恶劣 (awful), 恶意 (malice), 罪恶 (crime), 恶作剧 (a prank). Read ě in 恶心 (nauseating, to feel sick) and wù, it means to hate: 厌恶.

examples.hanzi: 他做了很多恶事。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò le hěn duō èshì.
examples.english: He did many evil things.

examples.hanzi: 他对邻居的态度很恶劣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì línjū de tàidù hěn èliè.
examples.english: His attitude toward the neighbors is very bad.

components.note: 方 (fāng) is a near sound match for páng (-ang); 方 also sounds out 房 fáng and 防 fáng.

example.hanzi: 他坐在我旁边。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò zài wǒ pángbiān.
example.english: He is sitting next to me.
example.fact: 旁 builds 旁边 (beside), 路旁 (roadside) and 旁人 (bystander). In studying characters, 偏旁 is the word for a radical or component, using 旁 for 'side'.

examples.hanzi: 马路旁种着很多树。
examples.pinyin: Mǎlù páng zhòng zhe hěn duō shù.
examples.english: Many trees are planted beside the road.

examples.hanzi: 他在旁观,没有说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài pángguān, méiyǒu shuōhuà.
examples.english: He watched from the sidelines without speaking.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).

example.hanzi: 他在家里是大哥,要照顾弟弟妹妹。
example.pinyin: Tā zài jiā lǐ shì dàgē, yào zhàogù dìdi mèimei.
example.english: He is the eldest brother in the family and has to look after his younger siblings.
example.fact: Beyond its literal family sense, 大哥 has become a common way to address a respected older male friend, a workplace senior, or even the head of a criminal gang — family vocabulary put to work as a marker of respect or hierarchy, the same extension seen in words like 老板 (“boss”) or 头儿 (“chief”).

examples.hanzi: 大哥，请问这条路能到火车站吗？
examples.pinyin: Dàgē, qǐngwèn zhè tiáo lù néng dào huǒchēzhàn ma?
examples.english: Brother, excuse me, does this road lead to the train station?

examples.hanzi: 我大哥比我大八岁，已经结婚了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dàgē bǐ wǒ dà bā suì, yǐjīng jiéhūn le.
examples.english: My eldest brother is eight years older than me and is already married.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
女 (woman) — marks women and girls, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 妞 is a girl.
丑 (chǒu) is only a loose sound hint for niū.

example.hanzi: 那个小妞跑得真快。
example.pinyin: Nàge xiǎoniū pǎo de zhēn kuài.
example.english: That little girl runs really fast.
example.fact: 妞 is used almost exclusively to name young girls, built from 女 (“woman”) plus the phonetic 丑 (chǒu) — a sound link that has faded further than most, since niū and chǒu barely rhyme after roughly three thousand years of pronunciation change. As a colloquial, Northern-Mandarin-flavored word, 小妞 can sound affectionate among friends or condescending coming from a stranger, depending entirely on tone of voice.

examples.hanzi: 这个小妞很聪明，什么都一学就会。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoniū hěn cōngmíng, shénme dōu yì xué jiù huì.
examples.english: This little girl is clever and picks up everything quickly.

examples.hanzi: 隔壁的小妞今年才五岁。
examples.pinyin: Gébì de xiǎoniū jīnnián cái wǔ suì.
examples.english: The little girl next door is only five this year.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 树, 林, 桥; 橄 is the olive tree (橄榄).
敢 (gǎn) gives the sound exactly: 橄 gǎn.
木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 树, 林, 桥; 榄 is the olive tree (橄榄).
览 (lǎn) gives the sound exactly: 榄 lǎn, also in 揽 lǎn and 缆 lǎn.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 美国人特别喜欢看橄榄球比赛。
example.pinyin: Měiguórén tèbié xǐhuan kàn gǎnlǎnqiú bǐsài.
example.english: Americans especially love watching football games.
example.fact: 橄榄球 literally means “olive ball” — 橄榄 (“olive”) is borrowed purely for its oval shape to name the sport's distinctively non-round ball, the same way an English speaker might informally describe an American football as “egg-shaped.”

examples.hanzi: 他很喜欢打橄榄球。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan dǎ gǎnlǎnqiú.
examples.english: He loves playing rugby.

examples.hanzi: 这个橄榄球是皮做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gǎnlǎnqiú shì pí zuò de.
examples.english: This rugby ball is made of leather.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.

example.hanzi: 药物进入体内后开始起作用。
example.pinyin: Yàowù jìnrù tǐnèi hòu kāishǐ qǐ zuòyòng.
example.english: Once the medicine enters the body, it starts to take effect.
example.fact: 内 pictures a person 人 stepping into an enclosure 冂 — literally “entering an enclosed space” — giving 体内 (“within the body”) a transparent, almost architectural logic, with the body treated as a container that has an inside and an outside, the same contrast captured by its opposite, 体外 (“outside the body,” used for lab work done outside a living organism).

examples.hanzi: 酒精进入体内会影响判断力。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔjīng jìnrù tǐnèi huì yǐngxiǎng pànduàn lì.
examples.english: Alcohol in the body affects your judgment.

examples.hanzi: 多运动可以增加体内的能量。
examples.pinyin: Duō yùndòng kěyǐ zēngjiā tǐnèi de néngliàng.
examples.english: Exercising more can increase energy in your body.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 拔 is pulling something out.
犮 (bá) — same sound: 拔 bá. 犮 also sounds out 跋 bá and 魃 bá.

example.hanzi: 他把草拔掉了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ cǎo bá diào le.
example.english: He pulled up the weeds.
example.fact: 拔 is to yank something out: 拔草 (weed), 拔牙 (extract a tooth), 拔河 (tug of war, literally 'pull river'). 挺拔 describes something tall and straight.

examples.hanzi: 他把萝卜拔出来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ luóbo bá chūlái le.
examples.english: He pulled the radish out.

examples.hanzi: 牙医把我的牙拔掉了。
examples.pinyin: Yáyī bǎ wǒ de yá bá diào le.
examples.english: The dentist pulled my tooth out.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是外星人入侵地球的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì wàixīngrén rùqīn dìqiú de gùshi.
example.english: This movie is about aliens invading Earth.
example.fact: 外星人 breaks down with unusual transparency into “outside” (外) + “star” (星) + “person” (人) — literally “a person from an outside star” — built the same way as its shorter cousin 外国人 (“foreigner,” literally “a person from an outside country”).

examples.hanzi: 你相信外星人真的存在吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiāngxìn wàixīngrén zhēnde cúnzài ma?
examples.english: Do you believe aliens really exist?

examples.hanzi: 孩子们画了一个绿色的外星人。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen huà le yí ge lǜsè de wàixīngrén.
examples.english: The kids drew a green alien.

meanings: when all is said and done

components.note: 比 (bǐ) — near sound — 毕 is bì; 比 also sounds out 毙 bì, so the shared syllable bì is easy to remember.
音 (sound) — a piece of music 音 played to its end by a person 儿: finishing, then "at last" or unexpectedly.

example.hanzi: 毕竟他还是个孩子,不能要求太高。
example.pinyin: Bìjìng tā háishi ge háizi, bù néng yāoqiú tài gāo.
example.english: After all, he's still a child, so we can't expect too much.
example.fact: 毕竟 typically opens a clause that reminds the listener of an underlying, easily-overlooked reason — much like English “after all” — and it pairs naturally with a following clause that softens an earlier claim or draws a more forgiving conclusion.

examples.hanzi: 虽然很累，但毕竟这是我们的工作。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dàn bìjìng zhè shì wǒmen de gōngzuò.
examples.english: Although it's tiring, this is our job after all.

examples.hanzi: 你别怪他，毕竟他也不是故意的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié guài tā, bìjìng tā yě bú shì gùyì de.
examples.english: Don't blame him; he didn't do it on purpose after all.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
广 (building) — marks halls and structures, as in 店 shop, 库 store, 座 seat; 廊 is a corridor.
郎 (láng) gives the sound exactly: 廊 láng, also in 狼 láng.

example.hanzi: 学生们在走廊里排队。
example.pinyin: Xuéshengmen zài zǒuláng lǐ páiduì.
example.english: The students are lining up in the corridor.
example.fact: 走 (a person swinging their arms while moving, from a stylized moving figure over 止 “a foot”) supplies the idea of passing through, while 廊 (广 “a building” plus the phonetic 郎, láng) names a covered walkway — together 走廊 literally suggests a “walking-building,” a structure built specifically for passing through.

examples.hanzi: 医院的走廊里有很多人在等候。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn de zǒuláng lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén zài děnghòu.
examples.english: There are many people waiting in the hospital corridor.

examples.hanzi: 请不要在走廊里大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào zài zǒuláng lǐ dàshēng shuō huà.
examples.english: Please don't talk loudly in the hallway.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil, ground and earthen things, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; a wall was packed earth.
啬 (sè) is only a loose sound hint for qiáng.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 墙上挂着一幅画。
example.pinyin: Qiángshang guà zhe yì fú huà.
example.english: A painting is hanging on the wall.
example.fact: 墙上 follows one of Mandarin's most productive patterns for saying “on/at [a place]” — attaching the light, neutral-toned 上 directly after a location noun, no preposition needed, the same pattern behind 桌上 (“on the table”), 身上 (“on the body”), and 路上 (“on the road”).

examples.hanzi: 他在墙上画了一幅画。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài qiángshang huà le yì fú huà.
examples.english: He painted a picture on the wall.

examples.hanzi: 一只小猫坐在墙上晒太阳。
examples.pinyin: Yì zhī xiǎo māo zuò zài qiángshang shài tàiyáng.
examples.english: A kitten sits on top of the wall sunbathing.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 痕; 症 is an illness or its symptoms.
正 (zhèng) — same sound — 症 is zhèng, like 正; 正 also sounds out 证 zhèng.
犬 (dog) — animals: 狗, 猫; 状 first meant the shape of an animal.
丬 (a form of 爿) gives zhuàng: also in 壮 zhuàng, 装 zhuāng, 将 jiāng and 奖 jiǎng.

example.hanzi: 医生问我有什么症状。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng wèn wǒ yǒu shénme zhèngzhuàng.
example.english: The doctor asked me what symptoms I had.
example.fact: 症 pairs the “sickness” radical 疒 (the same radical behind 发疯's 疯, also in this batch) with the phonetic 正 (zhèng, an exact sound match), while 状 contributes the sense of “condition, form” — together naming the visible “form a sickness takes,” which is exactly what a symptom is.

examples.hanzi: 这种病的主要症状是发烧和咳嗽。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng de zhǔyào zhèngzhuàng shì fāshāo hé késou.
examples.english: The main symptoms of this illness are fever and coughing.

examples.hanzi: 吃药以后，症状慢慢消失了。
examples.pinyin: Chī yào yǐhòu, zhèngzhuàng mànmàn xiāoshī le.
examples.english: After taking medicine, the symptoms slowly disappeared.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
衤 (clothing) — marks cloth and garments, as in 衬, 衫, 补; 初 pairs it with 刀 knife: cutting cloth was the first step in making clothes, hence 'beginning'.
刀 (knife) — the cutting tool, as in 分 divide, 切 cut.

example.hanzi: 我当初就不该答应这件事。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dāngchū jiù bù gāi dāying zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: I shouldn't have agreed to this in the first place.
example.fact: 当初 almost always signals hindsight — it frames a past moment specifically so the speaker can comment on how things have (or haven't) turned out since, which is why it shows up constantly in regret-tinged sentences built on the pattern “当初就不该...” (“shouldn't have... back then”).

examples.hanzi: 当初我们都没想到会这样。
examples.pinyin: Dāngchū wǒmen dōu méi xiǎngdào huì zhèyàng.
examples.english: At the time, none of us expected it to turn out this way.

examples.hanzi: 他当初是一个小店员，现在已经是经理了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngchū shì yí ge xiǎo diànyuán, xiànzài yǐjīng shì jīnglǐ le.
examples.english: He started out as a small shop assistant and is now a manager.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.
彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.

example.hanzi: 说谎是不道德的行为。
example.pinyin: Shuōhuǎng shì bù dàodé de xíngwéi.
example.english: Lying is an immoral act.
example.fact: 道德 joins two words that are each philosophically loaded on their own — 道 (“the Way,” a central concept in Daoist and Confucian thought referring to the natural or moral order of the universe) and 德 (“virtue,” inner moral character) — so unlike English “morality,” which traces back to Latin mores (“customs”), 道德 carries an explicit metaphysical undertone straight from classical Chinese philosophy.

examples.hanzi: 我们要遵守社会道德。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnshǒu shèhuì dàodé.
examples.english: We must follow social morals.

examples.hanzi: 他是个很有道德的人，从不占别人便宜。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge hěn yǒu dàodé de rén, cóng bú zhàn biéren piányi.
examples.english: He is a very ethical person who never takes advantage of others.

components.note: 目 (eye) — eyes and seeing: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睛 eyeball; sleep is when the eyes close.
垂 (chuí, droop) hints at the sound and the image: drooping eyelids. Also in 锤 chuí.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 他躺下没多久就睡着了。
example.pinyin: Tā tǎng xià méi duō jiǔ jiù shuìzháo le.
example.english: He fell asleep not long after lying down.
example.fact: 着 is one of Mandarin's most read-dependent characters: as zháo, attached after 睡, it marks a completed action (“succeeded in falling asleep”), while the very same character elsewhere serves as the toneless aspect particle zhe marking an ongoing action (as in 有着, also in this batch) — the correct reading depends entirely on grammatical role, with no visual cue in the character itself.

examples.hanzi: 孩子终于睡着了，请小声一点。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zhōngyú shuìzháo le, qǐng xiǎoshēng yìdiǎn.
examples.english: The child has finally fallen asleep, so please keep it down.

examples.hanzi: 昨晚太吵了，我一直没睡着。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn tài chǎo le, wǒ yìzhí méi shuìzháo.
examples.english: It was too noisy last night and I couldn't fall asleep.

components.note: 骨 (bone) — 骨 is the bone radical, as in 骼, 髓, 体; 骨 is bones, with ⺼ (flesh) beneath.

example.hanzi: 他的腿骨折了。
example.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ gǔzhé le.
example.english: His leg is broken.
example.fact: 骨 is bone: 骨头 (bone), 骨折 (fracture), 排骨 (ribs, a popular dish). It also gives the idea of backbone: 骨气 is moral courage, and 骨肉 means one's flesh and blood.

examples.hanzi: 小狗在啃骨头。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zài kěn gǔtou.
examples.english: The puppy is gnawing a bone.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的排骨很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de páigǔ hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The ribs at this restaurant are delicious.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 思, 爱; 慰 is to soothe the heart.
尉 (wèi) gives the sound exactly: 慰 wèi.

example.hanzi: 朋友难过时,我们应该安慰她。
example.pinyin: Péngyou nánguò shí, wǒmen yīnggāi ānwèi tā.
example.english: When a friend is sad, we should comfort her.
example.fact: 安 (a woman 女 sheltered safely under a roof 宀, giving the sense of “peace, safety”) pairs with 慰 (心 “heart” plus the phonetic 尉, wèi) to form 安慰 — literally something like “putting the heart at peace,” a compositional logic that maps almost directly onto its English translation “to comfort.”

examples.hanzi: 她哭得很伤心，我只好去安慰她。
examples.pinyin: Tā kū de hěn shāngxīn, wǒ zhǐhǎo qù ānwèi tā.
examples.english: She cried so sadly that I had to go comfort her.

examples.hanzi: 你的话给了我很大的安慰。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de huà gěi le wǒ hěn dà de ānwèi.
examples.english: Your words gave me great comfort.

components.note: 糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.
刂 (knife) — marks cutting and dividing, as in 别, 刻, 划; 列 is to split into rows, hence a line or list.
歹 (bone, death) — marks death and decay, as in 死, 残; 列 liè itself also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.

example.hanzi: 他提出了一系列新的想法。
example.pinyin: Tā tíchū le yí xìliè xīn de xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: He proposed a series of new ideas.
example.fact: 系列 is almost always preceded by 一 in the fixed phrase 一系列 (“a series of, a whole set of”) — 系 already carries a sense of “linking, connecting” (from 糸, thread or silk), so 系列 layers “linked” over “arranged in a row” (列) to picture items strung together in sequence.

examples.hanzi: 这个系列的电影一共有五部。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xìliè de diànyǐng yígòng yǒu wǔ bù.
examples.english: This series of movies has five films in total.

examples.hanzi: 学校组织了一系列有趣的活动。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zǔzhī le yíxìliè yǒuqù de huódòng.
examples.english: The school organized a series of interesting activities.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 这座城市有着悠久的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒuzhe yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
example.english: This city has a long and storied history.
example.fact: 有着 is functionally almost identical to plain 有 (“to have”), but the added particle 着 gives it a more literary, descriptive flavor suited to writing — it appears constantly in essays and formal descriptions (“有着...的历史/意义/特点”) but can sound stilted in casual speech, where bare 有 is the natural choice.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子有着一双明亮的大眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi yǒuzhe yì shuāng míngliàng de dà yǎnjing.
examples.english: This child has a pair of bright big eyes.

examples.hanzi: 他有着丰富的工作经验。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒuzhe fēngfù de gōngzuò jīngyàn.
examples.english: He has rich work experience.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).

example.hanzi: 这个孩子是全家的宝贝。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi shì quán jiā de bǎobèi.
example.english: This child is the whole family's treasure.
example.fact: 宝 is a treasure: 宝石 (gem), 国宝 (national treasure, such as the giant panda). 宝贝 and 宝宝 are affectionate words for children and for a lover. The e-commerce site Taobao (淘宝) is 'hunt for treasure'.

examples.hanzi: 他在海底找到了一个宝箱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hǎidǐ zhǎodào le yí ge bǎoxiāng.
examples.english: He found a treasure chest on the seabed.

examples.hanzi: 这座博物馆里有很多国宝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò bówùguǎn li yǒu hěn duō guóbǎo.
examples.english: This museum has many national treasures.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸 face, 腿 leg, 脑 brain; 肌 is muscle.
几 (jī) gives the sound exactly: 肌 jī, also in 机 jī and 饥 jī.
肉 — a picture of a slab of meat with its grain lines; as a left-hand radical it shrinks to ⺼ in 脸, 腿, 肌.

example.hanzi: 他经常锻炼,肌肉很发达。
example.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng duànliàn, jīròu hěn fādá.
example.english: He exercises regularly, so his muscles are well developed.
example.fact: 肌 (⺼ “flesh” plus the phonetic 几, jǐ) and 肉 (a pictograph of a cut of meat, its outline 冂 wrapping around lines 仌 that suggest muscle fiber or ribs) both independently mean roughly “flesh, meat” — 肌肉 doubles up two near-synonyms from the same semantic field into one specific, modern word for “muscle.”

examples.hanzi: 多运动，肌肉才会变得结实。
examples.pinyin: Duō yùndòng, jīròu cái huì biàn de jiēshi.
examples.english: Exercise more and your muscles will become firm.

examples.hanzi: 跑完步后，我的腿部肌肉很酸。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo wán bù hòu, wǒ de tuǐbù jīròu hěn suān.
examples.english: After running, my leg muscles are sore.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 起, 越, 赶: going toward something that attracts you.
取 (qǔ) is a close sound clue for qù; 取 also in 娶 qǔ and 聚 jù.

example.hanzi: 这本书很有趣。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒuqù.
example.english: This book is very interesting.
example.fact: 趣 mainly appears in 有趣 (interesting), 兴趣 (interest), 乐趣 (pleasure) and 趣事 (an amusing anecdote). The sentence 对…感兴趣 means to be interested in something.

examples.hanzi: 我对历史很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì lìshǐ hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in history.

examples.hanzi: 他讲话很风趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎnghuà hěn fēngqù.
examples.english: He speaks in a very witty way.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).

example.hanzi: 天气冷了,你要多保重身体。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì lěng le, nǐ yào duō bǎozhòng shēntǐ.
example.english: The weather's gotten cold — you should take good care of your health.
example.fact: 保重 is one of the most common ways to close a letter, phone call, or goodbye in Chinese, roughly matching English “take care” — 保 (a person 亻 looking after someone, historically a caretaker holding a child) plus 重 (“heavy, important”) suggests literally “guard what is important [your health].”

examples.hanzi: 路上小心，多保重！
examples.pinyin: Lùshang xiǎoxīn, duō bǎozhòng!
examples.english: Be careful on the road and take care of yourself!

examples.hanzi: 你工作那么忙，要保重身体。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gōngzuò nàme máng, yào bǎozhòng shēntǐ.
examples.english: You are so busy at work; take care of your health.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 这位科学家发现了一种新元素。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi kēxuéjiā fāxiàn le yì zhǒng xīn yuánsù.
example.english: This scientist discovered a new element.
example.fact: 家 as a suffix meaning “an expert or practitioner of X” turns 科学 (“science”) into 科学家 (“scientist”) the same way it turns 音乐 (“music”) into 音乐家 (“musician”) and 艺术 (“art”) into 艺术家 (“artist”) — one of Mandarin's most reliable, productive suffixes for naming a professional in a field.

examples.hanzi: 这位科学家获得了诺贝尔奖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi kēxuéjiā huòdé le Nuòbèi'ěr jiǎng.
examples.english: This scientist won a Nobel Prize.

examples.hanzi: 科学家们正在研究新的能源。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen zhèngzài yánjiū xīn de néngyuán.
examples.english: Scientists are researching new sources of energy.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.hanzi: 火车快要到站了。
example.pinyin: Huǒchē kuàiyào dào zhàn le.
example.english: The train is about to arrive at the station.
example.fact: 快要 almost always appears together with a sentence-final 了 to mark an imminent change of state, in the pattern “快要...了” (“about to...”) — the same “time adverb + 了” pairing that shows up with 已经 (“already”), making 了 one of the hardest-working single characters in Mandarin grammar.

examples.hanzi: 天快要黑了，我们回家吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiān kuàiyào hēi le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
examples.english: It's getting dark; let's go home.

examples.hanzi: 我快要毕业了，正在找工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kuàiyào bìyè le, zhèngzài zhǎo gōngzuò.
examples.english: I'm about to graduate and am looking for a job.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather, as in 雷 thunder, 雪 snow, 雾 fog; 震 is a quake, as when thunder shakes the ground.
辰 (chén) hints at the sound: 震 zhèn is close to 振 zhèn, which shares it.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.

example.hanzi: 这个消息让所有人都感到震惊。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi ràng suǒyǒu rén dōu gǎndào zhènjīng.
example.english: This news left everyone feeling shocked.
example.fact: 震 (雨 “rain” plus the phonetic 辰, chén) originally described thunder rumbling through a storm, while 惊 (忄 “heart” plus the phonetic 京, jīng — an exact sound match) names a startled emotional jolt — together 震惊 pairs a natural, physical shock with a psychological one.

examples.hanzi: 他的突然离开让大家都很震惊。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tūrán líkāi ràng dàjiā dōu hěn zhènjīng.
examples.english: His sudden departure shocked everyone.

examples.hanzi: 她震惊地看着眼前的一切。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhènjīng de kàn zhe yǎnqián de yíqiè.
examples.english: She stared at everything in front of her in shock.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 好; its link to 娱 (enjoyment) is historical, so lean on the sound part.
吴 (wú) hints at the sound: 娱 yú is close to 误 wù and 虞 yú.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".

example.hanzi: 周末我喜欢参加一些娱乐活动。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan cānjiā yìxiē yúlè huódòng.
example.english: On weekends I like to take part in some entertainment activities.
example.fact: 乐 is the simplified form of 樂, traditionally analyzed as a wooden instrument 木 strung with strings 幺 and played with a pick — music's association with joy gave 乐 its double life as both “happy” (lè) and “music” (yuè), two related but distinct readings of the same character depending on context.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市有很多娱乐场所。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu hěn duō yúlè chǎngsuǒ.
examples.english: This city has many entertainment venues.

examples.hanzi: 看电影是一种很好的娱乐方式。
examples.pinyin: Kàn diànyǐng shì yì zhǒng hěn hǎo de yúlè fāngshì.
examples.english: Watching movies is a good form of entertainment.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 按; 抗 is to resist or hold off.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound exactly: 抗 kàng, also in 炕 kàng.

example.hanzi: 人民奋起反抗压迫。
example.pinyin: Rénmín fènqǐ fǎnkàng yāpò.
example.english: The people rose up to resist oppression.
example.fact: 反 (a hand 又 pushing back against a cliff 厂, giving the sense of “to turn over, oppose”) and 抗 (a hand 扌 defending the throat 亢, a vulnerable point) both independently picture physical resistance — 反抗 doubles up two body-based images of pushing back into one word for active resistance.

examples.hanzi: 他们不愿意再忍受，决定反抗。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen bú yuànyì zài rěnshòu, juédìng fǎnkàng.
examples.english: They were unwilling to endure it any longer and decided to resist.

examples.hanzi: 小孩有时候会反抗父母的安排。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái yǒu shíhou huì fǎnkàng fùmǔ de ānpái.
examples.english: Children sometimes rebel against their parents' arrangements.

components.note: 王 (king/jade) — the middle part, as in 玉. Dictionary story: a jade statue with four holes (口) made in it, seen as a bad omen, so 噩梦 nightmare; memory aid.
口 (mouth) — four of them, dictionary radical. Memory aid: four mouths shouting around a king, a nightmare scene.
夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.

example.hanzi: 我昨晚做了一个噩梦。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn zuò le yí gè èmèng.
example.english: I had a nightmare last night.
example.fact: 噩 pictures repeated 口 (“mouth”) shapes, thought to represent cries of alarm or distress — stacking that ominous character directly onto 梦 (“dream,” built from eyes shut in sleep over 夕 “night”) gives 噩梦 a vivid, almost onomatopoeic image: a dream filled with screaming.

examples.hanzi: 别怕，那只是一个噩梦。
examples.pinyin: Bié pà, nà zhǐshì yí ge èmèng.
examples.english: Don't be afraid; it was only a nightmare.

examples.hanzi: 考试的前一天，我常常做噩梦。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì de qián yì tiān, wǒ chángcháng zuò èmèng.
examples.english: The day before an exam, I often have nightmares.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
火 (fire) — the bottom part, as in 灯 lamp and 炎 flame. The dictionary lists fire as the hint: a spirit like a flickering flame, as in 灵魂.
彐 (snout) — the top part, a stroke group as in 当 and 归. 灵 simplifies 靈, so this shape is not a sound clue. Memory aid: a hand over a flame, feeling a spirit.

example.hanzi: 音乐可以治愈人的心灵。
example.pinyin: Yīnyuè kěyǐ zhìyù rén de xīnlíng.
example.english: Music can heal the human soul.
example.fact: 心 is a pictograph of the physical shape of a heart, extended early on to also mean “mind, feelings”; 心灵 pairs it with 灵 (whose semantic root 火 “fire” ties back to ritual fires once used to try to communicate with spirits) to form a word that leans toward the more poetic, spiritual register of “soul” or “inner self,” distinct from the more everyday, emotional 心情 (“mood, feelings”).

examples.hanzi: 她是一个心灵手巧的人，什么都会做。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge xīnlíng shǒuqiǎo de rén, shénme dōu huì zuò.
examples.english: She is a clever and skilled person who can make anything.

examples.hanzi: 这本书触动了很多读者的心灵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū chùdòng le hěn duō dúzhě de xīnlíng.
examples.english: This book touched the hearts of many readers.

components.note: 广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 这是他应得的奖励。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì tā yīngdé de jiǎnglì.
example.english: This is the reward he deserves.
example.fact: 应得 combines 应 (“should, ought to” — also seen in 应该) with 得 (“to obtain, to get” — a hand 寸 reaching for a valuable shell 貝) to mean literally “ought to obtain,” giving Mandarin a compact single word for “deserve” where English needs a separate verb.

examples.hanzi: 你付出了这么多，这笔奖金是你应得的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fùchū le zhème duō, zhè bǐ jiǎngjīn shì nǐ yīngdé de.
examples.english: You put in so much effort; this bonus is what you deserve.

examples.hanzi: 他犯了错，这是他应得的惩罚。
examples.pinyin: Tā fàn le cuò, zhè shì tā yīngdé de chéngfá.
examples.english: He made a mistake, and this is the punishment he deserves.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 奶 is milk or a grandmother.
乃 (nǎi) sounds exactly like 奶.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang hē yì bēi niúnǎi.
example.english: I drink a glass of milk every morning.
example.fact: 奶 means milk: 牛奶 (cow's milk), 奶茶 (milk tea), 奶酪 (cheese). Doubled, 奶奶 is the term for a father's mother, whereas 外婆 is a mother's mother.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶今年八十岁了。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai jīnnián bāshí suì le.
examples.english: Grandma is eighty this year.

examples.hanzi: 婴儿需要喝奶粉。
examples.pinyin: Yīng'ér xūyào hē nǎifěn.
examples.english: Babies need to drink formula.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 掩 is to cover with the hand.
奄 (yǎn) gives the sound: 掩 yǎn, close to 淹 yān and 腌 yān.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.hanzi: 队员们互相掩护,安全撤退了。
example.pinyin: Duìyuánmen hùxiāng yǎnhù, ānquán chètuì le.
example.english: The team members covered for each other and retreated safely.
example.fact: 掩护 layers two "hand" actions together — 掩 ("to cover," hand radical 扌 + phonetic 奄) and 护 ("to protect," hand radical 扌 + 户 "door/household") — and the same word covers both a soldier physically shielding a comrade and, by extension, someone covering up another person's wrongdoing, much like English "cover for someone."

examples.hanzi: 警察用车子掩护群众撤离。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yòng chēzi yǎnhù qúnzhòng chèlí.
examples.english: The police used vehicles to shield the crowd as it evacuated.

examples.hanzi: 这些树木掩护了他们的行动。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shùmù yǎnhù le tāmen de xíngdòng.
examples.english: The trees covered their movements.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁, 钟; mirrors were polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 镜 is jìng; 竟 also sounds out 境 jìng.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 她站在镜子前梳头发。
example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài jìngzi qián shū tóufa.
example.english: She stood in front of the mirror combing her hair.
example.fact: 镜 pairs the metal radical 钅 with the phonetic 竟 (jìng) — a reminder that before glass mirrors became common, Chinese mirrors were disks of polished bronze, which is why the character for "mirror" is built on "metal" rather than "glass."

examples.hanzi: 这面镜子有点脏，需要擦一擦。
examples.pinyin: Zhè miàn jìngzi yǒudiǎn zāng, xūyào cā yi cā.
examples.english: This mirror is a bit dirty and needs a wipe.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子对着镜子做鬼脸。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi duì zhe jìngzi zuò guǐliǎn.
examples.english: The little kid is making faces at the mirror.

components.note: 目 (eye) — opening the eyes; also in 看 look, 眼 eye.
争 (zhēng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 挣 zhèng and 筝 zhēng.

example.hanzi: 他慢慢睁开了眼睛。
example.pinyin: Tā mànmàn zhēngkāi le yǎnjing.
example.english: He slowly opened his eyes.
example.fact: 睁 is used only for opening the eyes, the opposite of 闭 (bì). The idiom 睁一只眼闭一只眼 means 'open one eye, close the other', that is, to look the other way and let something pass.

examples.hanzi: 我困得睁不开眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kùn de zhēng bu kāi yǎnjing.
examples.english: I'm so sleepy I can't keep my eyes open.

examples.hanzi: 他睁大眼睛看着我。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhēng dà yǎnjing kàn zhe wǒ.
examples.english: He looked at me with wide eyes.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a lump of earth on the ground; as a radical it marks land and soil, as in 地, 城, 块, 墙.

example.hanzi: 花需要种在土里。
example.pinyin: Huā xūyào zhòng zài tǔ lǐ.
example.english: Flowers need to be planted in soil.
example.fact: 土 is earth: 泥土 (soil), 土地 (land), 土豆 (potato, literally 'earth bean'). It is also one of the Five Elements. As an adjective, 土 means unfashionable or countrified: 很土 is 'so uncool'.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里玩泥土。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi li wán nítǔ.
examples.english: The kids are playing in the mud in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 这里的土地很适合种菜。
examples.pinyin: Zhèli de tǔdì hěn shìhé zhòng cài.
examples.english: The land here is well suited to growing vegetables.
